name: Middle Finger Buttress - Right Side

pitch_detail.notes: Steep slab with a thin vertical crack.
Remaining pitches up the NW-facing cracks to the top; historically included a brief C1 aid move.

descent_text: From the top, traverse east along the ridge crest to the col southwest of the North Ridge and downclimb the 3rd-class north-slope gully back toward the approach trail.
approach: Most parties start at the Andrews Creek trailhead (trail 504) at the edge of the Pasayten Wilderness. Follow the valley about four miles to the usual first camp in the burned section, cross Andrews Pass, then join the Boundary Trail to Upper Cathedral Lake; the whole trip is roughly 17 miles with about 4,800 ft of gain. Camp near the lake, in the boulder-strewn basin under the north face of Amphitheater Mountain. Middle Finger Buttress is the larger buttress on the right as you look up from the lake; walk around the shore and scramble about 15 minutes to its base, then go to the right side of the buttress where this route starts.
overview: A longer, 7-pitch 5.9 (with a short C1 aid section historically) trad/aid line up the right side of Amphitheater's largest buttress, climbing cracks on its northwest side.
beta: Climbs cracks up the northwest side of the buttress; begins on a steep slab with a thin vertical crack, with the short crux on the 3rd pitch. Historically included a brief C1 aid section, though it may go free at the grade for strong parties. The route climbs cracks on the NW side of the buttress, starting on a steep slab with a thin vertical crack, with the crux on pitch 3.
gear: wide range of nuts and cams
face: North Face (Middle Finger Buttress, NW side)
